problem: Determine the value to which the infinite product \( C_\infty(n) = \prod_{0 < q < \infty \land q \neq n} \frac{1}{e^{\frac{i\pi q}{t}}-e^{\frac{i\pi n}{t}}} \) converges, where \( t, n \in \mathbb{N} \).

# Evaluating the Infinite Product $C_\infty(n)$

## Setting Up the Structure

Let me define $\omega = e^{i\pi/t}$, a **primitive $2t$-th root of unity**. The product becomes:

$$C_\infty(n) = \prod_{\substack{q=1,\, q \neq n}}^{\infty} \frac{1}{\omega^q - \omega^n}$$

**Key observation:** Since $\omega^{q+2t} = \omega^q$, the sequence $\{\omega^q\}_{q=1}^{\infty}$ is **periodic with period $2t$**, cycling through all $2t$-th roots of unity. The infinite product is therefore a repetition of a finite "period product" $P$.

## Computing the One-Period Product

Over one period, I need $\displaystyle\prod_{\substack{q=1,\,q\neq n}}^{2t}(\omega^q - \omega^n)$.

Since $x^{2t}-1 = \prod_{j=0}^{2t-1}(x-\omega^j)$, I have:

$$\prod_{\substack{j=0,\,j\neq n}}^{2t-1}(x-\omega^j) = \frac{x^{2t}-1}{x-\omega^n}$$

Evaluating at $x = \omega^n$ (a removable singularity):

$$\prod_{\substack{j=0,\,j\neq n}}^{2t-1}(\omega^n - \omega^j) = \left.\frac{d}{dx}(x^{2t}-1)\right|_{x=\omega^n} = 2t\;\omega^{n(2t-1)}$$

Since $\omega^{2t}=1$:

$$\omega^{n(2t-1)} = \omega^{2tn}\cdot\omega^{-n} = 1\cdot e^{-i\pi n/t} = e^{-i\pi n/t}$$

Now converting to the product over $q=1,\dots,2t$ (the same set of roots, just shifted indexing) and flipping each factor:

$$\prod_{\substack{q=1,\,q\neq n}}^{2t}(\omega^q - \omega^n) = (-1)^{2t-1}\cdot 2t\;e^{-i\pi n/t} = -2t\;e^{-i\pi n/t}$$

since $2t-1$ is **odd**.

## The Period Product

$$P = \prod_{\substack{q=1,\,q\neq n}}^{2t}\frac{1}{\omega^q - \omega^n} = \frac{1}{-2t\;e^{-i\pi n/t}} = -\frac{e^{i\pi n/t}}{2t}$$

## Convergence of the Infinite Product

After $k$ complete periods (i.e., $2tk$ terms), the partial product equals $P^k$. For any $t \in \mathbb{N}$:

$$|P| = \frac{1}{2t} \leq \frac{1}{2} < 1$$

Therefore:

$$\lim_{k\to\infty} P^k = 0$$

Any remaining incomplete period contributes only a bounded factor (each term has $|\omega^q - \omega^n| > 0$ and is bounded), so the full sequence of partial products also converges to $0$.

## Result

$$C_\infty(n) = \prod_{\substack{q=1,\,q\neq n}}^{\infty} \frac{1}{e^{i\pi q/t}-e^{i\pi n/t}} = 0$$

$$\boxed{0}$$
